messages:
sara: quick sanity check — when we aggregate soft labels for the new reranker validation set the global ndcg looks fine but slice-level variance is wild. thoughts? :thinking:

jia: can you paste the aggregation strategies you tried? mean of probs vs mean of logits vs majority-weighted?

sara: tried three: 1) prob-mean (avg softmax probs per doc), 2) logit-avg (avg pre-softmax logits then softmax), 3) top-k majority (treat top label per annotator then weighted majority).

mike: which metric shows the biggest swing? ndcg@10 or mrr?

sara: ndcg@10 moves ~0.7-1.1% relative across slices, mrr less consistent — some tails see +2% with logit-avg but core queries drop.

jia: this smells like reordering sensitivity for near-ties. logit-avg can exaggerate small margin differences. prob-mean is more conservative.

sara: agree. i also plotted per-query label entropy vs delta-ndcg and theres a correlation — high-entropy queries flip rank order across strategies.
oliver: do we have a reproducible small sample? want to eyeball a handful of flipped queries.
sara: yes, here's a quick export:
```csv
query_id,agg_strategy,doc_id,score,label_mean,label_std,top1_votes
q123,prob-mean,d789,2.12,0.62,0.28,2
q123,logit-avg,d456,2.15,0.61,0.27,1
q123,topk-major,d789,1.98,0.64,0.29,3
```

mike: can we run eval-bot's pairwise consistency check? i want to know if flipping is due to score tie-breakers or metric threshold effects.
eval-bot: running pairwise_consistency for thread 1766304321 with strategies [prob-mean,logit-avg,topk-major] — ETA ~7m. will post heatmap. :robot_face:

jia: also check label aggregation that treats annotator calibration: some annotators skew high. e.g., z-score per-annotator then back-transform to probs. might reduce systematic bias.
sara: good call. i did a quick per-annotator z-normalize then prob-mean — small improvement on tail slices.
oliver: what's the slice definition here? length? vertical? recency?
sara: slices: short queries (<3 tokens), long queries (>15 tokens), recency-heavy (docs published <30d), and transactional-intent tag. biggest disagreement in short queries and transactional.
mike: maybe short queries have less context so annotator judgment unstable; aggregation amplifies that. Could down-weight high-entropy queries or fallback to majority for short queries.
jia: or expose uncertainty to downstream ranking — if top two docs within margin, call for secondary rerank with cross-encoder or more conservative model.
sara: pragmatic options: A) keep prob-mean globally, B) use logit-avg only for core queries with low entropy, C) hybrid: per-slice strategy selected via small heldout.
eval-bot: pairwise_consistency completed. attached summary:
```text
strategy_pairs: prob-mean vs logit-avg: 12.3% of queries change relative ordering (mostly short queries)
prob-mean vs topk-major: 8.9% change (high-entropy and recency slices)
logit-avg vs topk-major: 14.6% change
most metric deltas concentrated in top-20% tail slices
```

mike: thanks. can you produce a mini-experiment: holdout 5k queries from each slice, pick the aggregation that maximizes ndcg@10 on that holdout per-slice, then eval global? want to see overfitting risk.
sara: will run that. timeline — a few hours. posting results to this thread when ready.
jia: also log per-query uncertainty score (e.g., label_std) to S3 with a schema so we can later correlate with production feedback.
sara: logged. s3://redwood-eval/softlabel-2026-03-20/entropy-schema-v1.csv

oliver: one last ask — add one sample per flipping query with original annotator comments (if any) so product can help adjudicate.
sara: will include comments when available. thanks all :thumbsup:
